learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 22 dollars and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Initial 13 miles per hour at 0.50 per mile cost 6.50 and retained 15.50. Set 15 miles: cost 7.50, retained 14.50. Changed to 0.70: cost 10.50, retained 11.50. End 30 miles cost 21 and retained 1. Home zero miles retained all 22. Restored 15 miles and 0.50.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 14.50, referenced visited 0.70 contrast leaving 11.50, explained fuel and wear costs grow with mileage. No tax or tips and illustrative per-mile costs explicitly stated.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Stacked retained and driving-cost bar matched numeric chips. At 30 miles and 0.70 cost, one-dollar retained label extended left of its tiny segment and was partially clipped; restored original case rendered cleanly.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: Independent overlap: no primary review or other judgments inspected before freeze.

prediction.reason: Concrete retained-pay choice distinguishes gross from net.

interaction.reason: Mileage and cost controls isolate two drivers and boundary cases.
interaction.evidence: Zero miles retains 22; maximum tested cost leaves 1.

payoff.reason: Reveal uses original arithmetic and observed alternative.

clarity.reason: Clear units and model caveat; retained bar label clips at tiny segment.
clarity.evidence: One-dollar label partly outside bar at high-cost endpoint.

transfer.reason: Useful general earnings principle is stated without a new application.
transfer.evidence: Costs of earning come out of gross pay; same delivery job only.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard mileage steps and endpoints worked; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Headline hourly pay exceeds money retained.

visualExplanation.reason: A fixed total splits visibly into retained and cost segments.

playfulness.evidence: Mileage slider and three cost choices.

practicalValue.reason: Directly supports comparing earnings after operating costs.
practicalValue.evidence: Fuel and wear examples and explicit no-tax assumptions.

depth.reason: One multiplication and subtraction model with assumptions.
depth.evidence: Miles times cost per mile subtracted from pay.

complexity.reason: Everyday monetary arithmetic with simple controls.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish revenue from earnings after variable costs.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One mileage slider and three per-mile options.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Fuel and vehicle wear as earning costs.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Dollars per hour, miles per hour and dollars per mile.

whyCool: A headline hourly rate becomes a visibly divided cost-and-earnings bar.
caveat: Illustrative fixed gross pay excludes tax, tips and other time costs; narrow retained segment clips its label at tested maximum cost.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
